title: Hold jobs on low disk, resumable in place, default 10G minimum
summary: Retry job 20261017-001109-qfax: add a min-free-disk check (default 10G in config.rs) before dispatch and before the checks; clean terminal and idle workspaces' target/, and if still low hold the job as 'environment: low disk' instead of rejecting it. A held job resumes as the same job on a later drain, with its marker cleared, never via `athena retry`. Audience: the user running drain.

defaults_applied.how: New tests for each hold and resume path; cargo test, clippy and fmt must be clean.
Criteria run the tests that show cleanup, hold, resume and marker clearing happening.
The resume route is designed for both stages instead of leaving it open.
Docs and changelog describe the setting and the status for an outside reader.
The disk check is enforced in code at both stages, not by prose.
One focused change on the disk guard and its resume paths.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: keep jobs from failing when the disk fills; audience is the user running drain, who reads drain output and status.
The 10G default lives in config.rs and applies when the setting is absent; athena.toml stays untouched (per the user's earlier correction). The config digest is reset as needed.
Deleting a closed job's target/ already landed in 173d12e; only the idle sweep and the low-disk path are new.

Resume routes are settled in the plan: a dispatch-stage hold leaves the job Proposed and it runs on a later drain; a pre-checks hold leaves it Dispatched with a marker, and the next drain re-lists it through the interrupted-work listing, clears the marker and continues the same job. A held item ends its work in the current drain and is retried in the next drain, and the drain note says so.
state.rs and status.rs are in scope because the marker and the status label live there.
Re-running job 20261016-044847-hem1 stays a separate follow-up.

acceptance_criteria.text: With free disk simulated below the minimum, a test shows cleanup runs before dispatch and before the checks. Run `cargo test --locked`.

A test shows that when space is still low after cleanup at dispatch, the job is held with status 'environment: low disk', stays Proposed, is not rejected, and the user is told the free and required amounts. A later drain runs the same job once space is free. Run `cargo test --locked`.

A drain test goes through the real RealSteps::run mapping with a constant-low fake and a real LowDisk error from `go`. It asserts held == true and no failure counted. Then, after space returns, the same job (no new job id) reaches checks and a verdict, its marker is cleared, and status no longer shows it held. Run `cargo test --locked`.

A test shows a verification-stage hold ends the item's work in that drain and the job is listed again as interrupted by the interrupted-work listing on the next drain. The drain note says it will be tried on the next drain. `athena retry` is not the resume route. Run `cargo test --locked`.
A test shows the idle-workspace sweep removes target/ from idle workspaces, leaves source files, and skips workspaces whose job lock is held. Run `cargo test --locked`.

config.rs defines a 10G minimum-free-disk default used when the setting is absent, a test shows it parses, and the config digest is reset. athena.toml is unchanged. README and CHANGELOG name the setting and the 'environment: low disk' status, and say 'the user' rather than 'the operator'.
`cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` is clean and `cargo fmt --all --check` passes.

out_of_scope: Deleting a closed job's target/ (already landed in 173d12e)
departures: Larger than the reference: the change touches drain, run, state and status with a new resume path and many tests, and the last attempt failed in planning.
